title: Validation of Human Papillomavirus Assays and Collection Devices for Self-samples and Urine Samples
brief_summary: The VALHUDES study is a Diagnostic Test Accuracy study that aims to document the clinical accuracy of hrHPV testing on urine samples, collected under standardised and optimised conditions, and on two types of vaginal self-samples and compare results with those from matching samples taken by a clinician.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women with previous abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
* Women between the ages of 25 and 64

Exclusion Criteria:

* Hysterectomised women
* Women with known pregnancy
* Non-consenting women
* Women that are not able to understand and to sign the informed consent
study_population: 500 women referred to a participating Belgian colposcopy centre (University Hospital of Ghent, Brussels and Antwerp, Hospital of Tienen) because of a previous abnormal cervical cancer screening test result, will be enrolled after obtaining informed consent.
